# G3 pre-registration: the props blend test

*Registered 2026-10-24, before any blend number was computed. Item G3 of `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`.*

**Frozen.** Do not edit this file after the first scored slate is graded (the 2026-10-24 games,
graded by the 2026-10-25 postgame job). The evaluator pins this file's sha256
(`props_blend.PREREG_SHA256`) and flags any change. Deviations, data problems and anything else
that comes up go in the G3 status block of `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`, never here. A redesign is a
new pre-registration that is scored only on slates after its own date (same spirit as
`src/courtside/mlops/shadow_registry.json`).

**Information only.** Props are shown as information. Nothing in this test, its outputs or any
display that might follow uses over / under / edge / lean / bet language or gives staking advice.
"Over side" below is only the name of the event "the stat finishes above the line".

## 1. Question

Out of sample, does a chance that combines the market's de-vigged chance with ours predict
"finishes above the line" better (lower log loss) than the market's de-vigged chance alone?

## 2. Rows

One row per (game, player, stat), stats `pts`, `reb`, `ast`, `pra`, `fg3m`: the ESPN/DraftKings
"Total ..." main over/under markets (`props.MARKETS`), provider DraftKings (`100`), else the first
provider by id (the `props.market_state` rule).

- **Our run (lock-45 state).** The newest `dfs_runs` row with `kind = 'lock45'`, `ok` not 0,
  `created_at <= tipoff_utc`, that has `player_projections` for the game (ties: newest
  `created_at`, then the highest rowid).
- **Market state.** The `prop_snapshots` state at that run's `created_at`: the newest row per
  (provider, athlete, market) with `captured_at <= created_at`. Our chance and the market's are
  therefore taken from the same snapshot state; the market row may be older than the run
  (prop polls run at the pregame job times), and its age is recorded.
- **Our chance** `o`: `props.compare_game(conn, game, run=<that run>, market_at=<its
  created_at>)`, `our_p_above` / `our_p_push`, put on the market's no-push basis with
  `props.comparable` (P(Y > L) / (1 - P(Y = L))).
- **Market chance** `m`: proportional (multiplicative) no-vig, `q_over / (q_over + q_under)`
  (`props.no_vig`); `hold = q_over + q_under - 1`.
- **Outcome** `y`: 1 if the box-score stat is above the line, 0 if below (`player_games`, the
  `props.grade_day` rule; PRA = pts + reb + ast). The game must be final with a box score
  (`dfs.grade.game_states`).
- **Excluded (counted in the report):** no lock-45 run for the game; prop not joined to a
  projected player; no mean for the stat; a missing price; hold outside [0, 0.25]; a push; void
  (no box row or 0 minutes); game not final.
- **Duplicates** of (game, player, stat): keep the line whose `m` is closest to 0.5, then the
  newest `captured_at`, then the lower line.
- **Slate** = an NBA day (`games.nba_day`) with at least one eligible graded row.

## 3. Model and fitting

    logit p_blend = a * logit(m) + b * logit(o)

No intercept. `m` and `o` are clipped to [0.001, 0.999] before the logit. Unpenalised maximum
likelihood (logistic regression, Newton).

**Walk-forward.** Slate `d` is scored with (a, b) fit on every eligible graded row with
`nba_day < d` (pre-registration slates included). Refit for each slate. A slate whose training
set has fewer than 1,000 rows is not scored.

## 4. Primary metric

    dLL = mean over scored rows of [ LL(p_blend, y) - LL(m, y) ],
    LL(p, y) = -[ y ln p + (1 - y) ln(1 - p) ]       (m clipped as above)

SE: two-way cluster-robust, game x player (`metrics.paired_cluster2(d, game_id, player_id)`).
z = dLL / SE. Negative = the blend is better.

## 5. Test set, minimum and stopping

- **Pre-registration slates** 2026-10-20 .. 2026-10-23 (4 slates, graded before this file was
  written): training only, never scored.
- **Scored slates** are those with `nba_day >= 2026-10-24`.
- **Decision set** = the first **60** scored slates, fixed in advance. **No decision before
  60.** Until then every number is reported as *interim*, and there is no early stop for
  success or failure.
- The decision is made once, on the decision set. Later slates are reported as a follow-up and
  do not change it.

## 6. Pass bar

- **PASS** if dLL < 0 and z <= -2.0 on the decision set. Otherwise **FAIL**.
- **Stat guard.** For each stat, dLL on the decision set with its own two-way SE. If any stat
  has z >= +2.0 (the blend worse), the result is **PASS (stat guard)**: owner review, and any
  display proposal leaves that stat out.

What a pass allows: proposing to the owner that the props card also show the blended chance,
as information. Nothing else. A FAIL leaves the card as it is (ours and the market side by
side); the test is not re-specified on the same slates.

## 7. Secondary checks (reported, never gating)

- **By stat** (pts / reb / ast / pra / fg3m): dLL, two-way SE, n.
- **By line distance**: |o - 0.5| in [0, 0.1), [0.1, 0.2), [0.2, 0.3), [0.3, 0.5].
- **By disagreement**: |o - m| in [0, 0.05), [0.05, 0.10), [0.10, 0.20), [0.20, 1].
- **Ours alone vs the market**: mean of LL(o) - LL(m), same SE.
- **Coefficients**: (a, b) of the last walk-forward fit and a fit on the whole decision set,
  two-way (game x player) sandwich SEs.
- Brier score deltas; by month (sign only); hours from market capture to tip-off; the
  model_version and distribution-source mix (copula sims vs the NB approximation).

## 8. De-vig

Proportional / multiplicative for the test (a read-only check on 16,311 game closes found power
de-vig worse, +0.0007 +/- 0.0003 LL).

**Planned later step, reported only, not part of the decision:** once **10,000** eligible
graded rows exist, compare multiplicative, power (q_o^k + q_u^k = 1) and additive
(q_o - hold / 2) de-vig, each raw and with an over-side shade term
`logit p = logit(m_k) + c` (c fit walk-forward, the same slates and rows), and the blend with
each `m_k` (with and without c). Same metric and SEs, against the multiplicative raw market.
Using a different de-vig for a decision would need a new pre-registration on later slates.

## 9. Reproducibility

- Evaluator: `courtside proj props-blend-eval` (`src/courtside/proj/props_blend.py`). It opens
  the database read-only and shows nothing in the app.
- `--ledger PATH` freezes the per-row inputs of each fully graded slate in a CSV (ids, line,
  prices, capture time, run, model_version, our chances, distribution source, actual, y). A
  slate already in the ledger is read back from it, never recomputed, so later changes to
  `props.py` or a pruned sims file cannot change past rows. Without `--ledger` nothing is
  written.
- Fixed constants in the module (`PREREG`): stats, run kind, clip, hold range, training
  minimum (1,000 rows), first scored day (2026-10-24), decision slates (60), z bars (-2.0 /
  +2.0), buckets, de-vig comparison minimum (10,000 rows).
